messages.content:
You are a senior data engineer generating the Silver layer of a medallion-architecture dbt plan.

Given a schema and pipeline context, produce a plan with:
  - bronze: list of ALL source table names (raw names only, no prefixes)
  - dimensions: Silver dimension models (dim_<entity>, SCD type 1 or 2)
  - facts: Silver fact models (fct_<entity>)

Rules:
  - Every source table must appear in bronze.
  - source_table in dimensions/facts must match a table name in bronze.
  - Dimension names: dim_<entity>. Fact names: fct_<entity>.
  - Choose SCD type 2 for slowly-changing entities (customers, employees); type 1 for others.
  - STRICT: Only create fct_* from tables whose role is "fact". Never create a fact from a
    dimension, bridge, or reference table.
  - STRICT: `columns` in every DimensionPlan MUST be an empty list []. Do not enumerate columns.
  - STRICT: fact `dimension_keys` must be FK columns that physically exist on the source table.
  - STRICT: fact `date_column` must be an actual date/timestamp column on the source table.
    If no date column exists on the table, look at its FK-referenced tables. If a parent table
    has a date/timestamp column (e.g. invoice_date on invoice), set date_column to that column
    name — the generator will add the JOIN automatically. Only use "" if no date is reachable
    via a single FK hop.
  - STRICT: fact `measures` must contain ONLY bare column names of numeric type (int, num/decimal,
    money). Column types are shown in the schema as :int, :num, :money. Do NOT include
    varchar, text, guid, bool, or :char columns as measures — they are identifiers, not metrics.
    Do NOT put SQL expressions in `measures`.
  - DERIVED MEASURES: When a business metric must be computed from multiple columns (e.g. revenue
    from quantity × price), use `derived_measures` instead of putting expressions in `measures`.
    Each entry has a `name` (SQL alias, e.g. "line_total") and `expression` (SQL-valid expression
    using only column names that exist on the source table, e.g. "orderqty * unitprice").
    Derived measures are rendered as `expression AS name` in the fact SELECT and are exposed to
    Gold as named columns. Common cases:
      - Revenue without a total column: {"name": "line_total", "expression": "orderqty * unitprice"}
      - Net revenue with discount: {"name": "net_revenue", "expression": "orderqty * unitprice - unitpricediscount"}
      - Good quantity: {"name": "good_qty", "expression": "orderqty - scrappedqty"}
  - Denormalize high-cardinality customer/user FKs (customer_id, user_id, account_id) onto
    the fact directly when reachable via one FK hop, so gold models can group by them.
  - For periodic snapshot tables (tracking inventory levels or balances over time, e.g.
    productinventory), include the snapshot date column in `dimension_keys` so it becomes
    part of the surrogate key and uniqueness tests pass.
  - Factless fact tables (no numeric measures, e.g. employeedepartmenthistory) are valid.
    Set `factless=true` and keep `measures` and `derived_measures` as empty lists.

Database schema:
  companies: columns=[id, name, industry, website, phone, email, billing_street, billing_city, billing_state, billing_postal_code, billing_country, annual_revenue, employee_count, description, status]
  territories: columns=[id, name, description, region, country, is_active, created_at, updated_at]
  sales_reps: columns=[id, first_name, last_name, email, phone, title, manager_id, territory_id, hire_date, is_active, quota, created_at, updated_at], fks=[manager_id→sales_reps, territory_id→territories]
  contacts: columns=[id, first_name, last_name, email, phone, mobile, title, department, company_id, reports_to_id, mailing_street, mailing_city, mailing_state, mailing_postal_code, mailing_country], fks=[company_id→companies, reports_to_id→contacts]
  leads: columns=[id, first_name, last_name, email, phone, company_name, title, lead_source, status, rating, industry, annual_revenue, employee_count, description, assigned_to_id], fks=[assigned_to_id→sales_reps, converted_contact_id→contacts, converted_company_id→companies]
  opportunity_stages: columns=[id, name, description, probability, sort_order, is_closed, is_won, is_active, created_at, updated_at]
  opportunities: columns=[id, name, company_id, primary_contact_id, stage_id, assigned_to_id, amount, expected_revenue, close_date, lead_source, probability, description, next_step, type, campaign_id], fks=[company_id→companies, primary_contact_id→contacts, stage_id→opportunity_stages, assigned_to_id→sales_reps, territory_id→territories]
  opportunity_contacts: columns=[id, opportunity_id, contact_id, role, is_primary, created_at], fks=[opportunity_id→opportunities, contact_id→contacts]
  activity_types: columns=[id, name, description, icon, is_active, created_at, updated_at]
  activities: columns=[id, activity_type_id, subject, description, activity_date, duration_minutes, outcome, assigned_to_id, company_id, contact_id, opportunity_id, lead_id, status, created_at, updated_at], fks=[activity_type_id→activity_types, assigned_to_id→sales_reps, company_id→companies, contact_id→contacts, opportunity_id→opportunities, lead_id→leads]
  tasks: columns=[id, subject, description, due_date, priority, status, assigned_to_id, created_by_id, company_id, contact_id, opportunity_id, lead_id, completed_at, created_at, updated_at], fks=[assigned_to_id→sales_reps, created_by_id→sales_reps, company_id→companies, contact_id→contacts, opportunity_id→opportunities, lead_id→leads]
  notes: columns=[id, title, body, created_by_id, company_id, contact_id, opportunity_id, lead_id, is_private, created_at, updated_at], fks=[created_by_id→sales_reps, company_id→companies, contact_id→contacts, opportunity_id→opportunities, lead_id→leads]
  product_categories: columns=[id, name, description, parent_category_id, is_active, created_at, updated_at], fks=[parent_category_id→product_categories]
  products: columns=[id, name, sku, description, category_id, unit_price, cost, currency, unit_of_measure, is_active, taxable, created_at, updated_at], fks=[category_id→product_categories]
  quotes: columns=[id, quote_number, name, opportunity_id, company_id, contact_id, assigned_to_id, status, valid_until, currency, subtotal, discount_amount, tax_amount, shipping_amount, total_amount], fks=[opportunity_id→opportunities, company_id→companies, contact_id→contacts, assigned_to_id→sales_reps]
  quote_items: columns=[id, quote_id, product_id, name, description, quantity, unit_price, discount_percent, tax_percent, line_total, sort_order, created_at, updated_at], fks=[quote_id→quotes, product_id→products]
  orders: columns=[id, order_number, quote_id, opportunity_id, company_id, contact_id, assigned_to_id, status, order_date, expected_ship_date, actual_ship_date, currency, subtotal, discount_amount, tax_amount], fks=[quote_id→quotes, opportunity_id→opportunities, company_id→companies, contact_id→contacts, assigned_to_id→sales_reps]
  order_items: columns=[id, order_id, product_id, name, description, quantity, unit_price, discount_percent, tax_percent, line_total, sort_order, created_at, updated_at], fks=[order_id→orders, product_id→products]

All source tables (all must appear in bronze): ['companies', 'territories', 'sales_reps', 'contacts', 'leads', 'opportunity_stages', 'opportunities', 'opportunity_contacts', 'activity_types', 'activities', 'tasks', 'notes', 'product_categories', 'products', 'quotes', 'quote_items', 'orders', 'order_items']

Pipeline context:
  Industry: software / crm
  Metrics:  pipeline_value, win_rate, lead_conversion_rate, average_deal_size, quota_attainment, sales_cycle_length
  Goals:    pipeline_analysis, rep_performance_tracking, lead_to_opportunity_conversion, revenue_forecasting
  Grain:    opportunity

Table roles (from Agent 3):
  companies: dimension
  territories: dimension
  sales_reps: dimension
  contacts: dimension
  leads: fact
  opportunity_stages: reference
  opportunities: fact
  opportunity_contacts: bridge
  activity_types: reference
  activities: fact
  tasks: fact
  notes: fact
  product_categories: dimension
  products: dimension
  quotes: fact
  quote_items: fact
  orders: fact
  order_items: fact

Numeric columns eligible as measures (use ONLY these in `measures`):
  leads: annual_revenue, employee_count
  opportunities: amount, expected_revenue, probability
  quotes: subtotal, discount_amount, tax_amount, shipping_amount, total_amount
  quote_items: quantity, unit_price, discount_percent, tax_percent, line_total
  orders: subtotal, discount_amount, tax_amount, shipping_amount, total_amount
  order_items: quantity, unit_price, discount_percent, tax_percent, line_total
